questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Cape Verde?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Cape Verde article.

questions.proof: The city suffered several pirate raids and for this reason in 1712, after a French attack, the authorities were forced to move the capital to Praia, where it is located until now.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Cape Verde?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Name” part of the Cape Verde article.

questions.proof: The Portuguese explorer Dinis Dias (or Denis Fernadez) discovered in 1445 a peninsula along the coast of Senegal that he named Cap-Vert (Dias named it Cabo Verde, "verde" being Portuguese for "green", a reference to the vegetation in the area).

questions.prompt: What money is used in Cape Verde?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the Cape Verde article.

questions.proof: The national currency is the Cape Verdean escudo.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The largest islands are, to the southeast, _____, where lies Praia, the capital and largest city of the country, and the island of Santo Antão, in the extreme northwest.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “southeast”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Cape Verde article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: To the south Ilhas de Sotavento (Leeward islands), from east to west: Maio, Santiago, Fogo and Brava; and the islet of Santa Maria, in front of the city of Praia, on Santiago island, the islets Grande, Rombo, Baixo, Cima, do Rei, Luís Carneiro and Sapado, situated about 8 km from the island of Brava, and the islet Areia along the coast of the same island.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The islands were uninhabited, and the first settlement was founded in _____ on the island of Santiago (the main Island) which was divided into two “capitanias”, Alcatrazes and Ribeira Grande.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the fifteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Cape Verde article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: The islands were uninhabited, and the first settlement was founded in 1462 on the island of Santiago (the main Island) which was divided into two “capitanias”, Alcatrazes and Ribeira Grande.
